title: Who wrote what: 'Poor Little Me', 'Saratoga Shout' and 'Saratoga Drag'
summary: Holmes says 'Poor Little Me' was Barbarin's, he and Greely Walton wrote the Saratoga numbers, and everyone contributed for love of the life.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, didn't you write your own composition, 'Poor Little Me' at about this time?
That's not mine. That's Paul Barbarin's.
You play soprano on that. But you wrote a number, though. Didn't you write 'Saratoga Drag'?

Greeley wrote 'Saratoga Drag.' 'Saratoga Shout'. I have to stop and think of the name of it myself, and I still don't know what it sounds like. I've got it, but I don't remember. Well, most of the numbers...
I mean, everybody was contributing to the band at this time.

Well, yeah, yeah. There was nobody in it for no money. We was doin' it because of the love of the life. You know what I mean? I liked it. I liked it! There was no money guaranteed. You like it at your own risk. If you want it... You wrote it because you wanted to
hear it. It wasn't ...(?)..., but it was enjoyable. Very enjoyable.
